name: cmux.widget/1
docs: A glanceable widget, as on an iPhone or a Mac desktop: a tile the person places on the New Tab page's widget grid or in the sidebar (Edit Widgets > Add Widget), in one of the sizes the widget offers. cmux ships no widgets of its own; every widget is an installed extension's, and an extension never places itself. Sizes are tiles of one grid: small is 1x1, medium 2x1, large 2x2; the sidebar takes small and medium at its width. The render export gets the mount context {surface: "widget", place: "newtab" | "sidebar", size, instance, settings, refresh: {everySeconds} | null, locale, timeZone, now()}: `instance` is stable for the placed tile (keep state that must outlive the app in cmux.storage under it), `settings` are the tile's own (an object, empty until set), `locale` (BCP 47) and `timeZone` (IANA) are the person's, from the page that shows the tile (the sandbox has no Intl: name the local zone with `timeZone`, and get its offset with cmux.time.zone), and `now()` is a reactive clock in milliseconds that the host ticks. The host owns the timer: `options.refresh.everySeconds` is raised to at least 60 and ticks on wall-clock boundaries (a 60 s clock ticks on the minute), only while the tile is shown; a hidden page or a scrolled-away tile gets no tick and catches up with one tick when it shows. Outside the few seconds after a mount, a tick or the person's tap, a widget's scene updates are coalesced to at most one every 15 s, and edit mode shows the count it held back. Read data through cmux.watch signals (cached and shared) in a render that reads now(), not with your own timers. A resize remounts the tile at its new size. Clicks run the node's onTap with the app's own scopes. Nodes outside `nodes` are refused and a scene over `maxNodes` stops drawing: the tile shows the widget's name and why.

sizes.description: The sizes the widget draws, as Apple's widget families: small (1x1 tile), medium (2x1), large (2x2). Default: ["small"].

defaultSize.description: The size Add Widget places first; one of `sizes`. Default: the first of `sizes`.

everySeconds.description: How often `now()` ticks. The host raises it to at least 60 and aligns ticks to the wall clock.

refresh.description: The host-owned tick. Without it the widget redraws only when its signals change.

places.description: Where the person can place the widget: the New Tab page's grid, the sidebar, or both. Default: both. The App Store shows it as "Shows up in".

status: draft: shapes are refined with the first implementing app before the interface is public
